title: Epochal audit index with immutable snapshots and residency-aware exports
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers and auditors require tamper-evident, residency-aware exports of admin and access audit events with verifiable proofs and small retrieval latency. Current audit export flows rely on infrequent bulk dumps and lack a compact proof-of-inclusion layer, making on-demand attestation and legal/retention gating slow and fragile.

Goals:
- Provide epochal immutable snapshots of admin/access/config-change events that are storage-efficient and queryable without breaking WORM guarantees.
- Surface a signed export manifest (root hash + sequence ranges) that customers and internal compliance teams can verify independently.
- Respect data residency and retention controls at export time: ensure exports only include events allowed by region/retention policy, and automatically redact or flag ineligible events.
- Automation for scheduled and ad-hoc evidentiary exports with delivery channels (S3 WORM bucket, customer KMS-wrapped archive, secure transfer), and attach cryptographic proofs (Merkle inclusion proofs) for sampled queries.

Proposed design summary:
1) Ingest path: audit events (admin actions, auth/assume-role, config diffs) stream to an append-only local WAL per-region. Each region maintains an epoch counter (epoch = UTC midnight or configurable window).
2) Epochal snapshotter: at epoch boundary the snapshotter compacts the WAL into a content-addressed segment: compressed newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) with an embedded event index (offsets) and a Merkle tree computed over canonicalized event bytes. The segment receives an immutable object name with the sequence range and region tag. The object is written to the configured object-store path with immutability/retention flags applied (vendor-specific, e.g., S3 Object Lock / GCS Retention).
3) Signed export manifest: a small JSON manifest (epoch, region, segment_ids, merkle_root, sequence_min, sequence_max, retention_policy_id, retention_until) is signed by Redwood platform signing key. Optionally customers with dedicated/private deployments can supply a customer signing key for additional attestations.
4) Queryable index: build a compact per-epoch prefix index (Bloom + minimal Merkle proofs precomputed for sampled ranges) stored separately in a read-optimized store to satisfy low-latency 'show me events for GRANT role X between T1 and T2' without scanning full WORM segments. Proofs reference merkle_root in the signed manifest. Index entries contain event sequence ids and segment pointer.
5) Residency and retention gating: snapshotter consults residency ruleset and retention matrix to determine which events are eligible for export. Ineligible events are either redacted (keeping sequence placeholder and redaction tag) or excluded from export depending on policy; the manifest records redaction decisions and counts.
6) Exports and delivery: automation supports three modes: scheduled archival to customer-designated WORM bucket (with optional KMS wrap), ad-hoc evidentiary export for compliance requests, and automated periodic attestations to a validator endpoint (internal or customer). All exports include manifest + per-request signed receipt with root and object checksums.

Trade-offs considered:
- Precomputing Merkle proofs vs on-demand proof generation: precompute increases snapshot size modestly but gives fast verification for auditors; we chose precompute for typical compliance SLAs.
- Storing compact index outside WORM: index must be queryable and fast; keeping it outside WORM is acceptable if we store final pointers and signed manifests in WORM to prevent tampering.
- Redaction vs exclusion: redaction preserves sequence continuity and tamper-evidence at cost of storing placeholder bytes; exclusion risks gaps and complicates inclusion proofs. We prefer redaction when retention rules require event suppression.

Migration plan from current exports:
- Phase 0 (week 1-2): feature flagged test pipeline in staging that writes epoch segments and manifests for a subset of audit streams.
- Phase 1 (week 3-5): read-path tooling: verify clients can validate manifests and inclusion proofs; build UI in Console to display epoch list and manifest details.
- Phase 2 (week 6-8): region-by-region rollout; mirror existing bulk exports to S3 while simultaneously producing epoch segments for parity verification.
- Phase 3 (week 9+): cutover export workflows (stop old bulk dumps), enable scheduled customer exports, and enable retention-enforced deletions for qualifying ranges.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests for canonicalization, merkle tree correctness, and manifest signing.
- Integration tests that assert proof-of-inclusion for sampled events across storage backends.
- Chaos test: simulate node restarts during snapshotting to ensure WAL replay and idempotent writes.
- Compliance verification runbook: automated verification job that fetches manifest, downloads one segment per epoch, validates signatures and merkle proofs, and posts a pass/fail to the compliance dashboard.

Rollout and monitoring:
- Feature flag gating per-customer and per-region.
- Metric surfaces: snapshot size, manifest signing latency, proof validation latency, export success rate, redaction counts, and export delivery time.
- Alerts: failed snapshot writes, manifest-signing errors, high redaction rate (>5% sustained), and retention-policy mismatches.

Open decisions / questions for PM/security/ops:
- Customer-managed signing keys: support HSM-backed key material for private deployments or rely on Redwood-signed manifests by default? (security team preference requested)
- Retention policy UI: should the Console expose a simulation mode showing how retention rules would affect a historical export? (PM asks for early mockups)
- Index durability SLA: how resilient must the read-optimized index be vs rebuild cost from WORM segments? (ops input needed)

Dependencies and blocking items:
- Object-store immutability API availability per cloud region (ops to confirm for new APAC regions).
- Security review for signing key management and trust model (security team).
- Console UI slots for export manifest and proof visualization (product + design).

Links and artifacts:
- Spec: https://company-confluence/internal/compliance/epochal-audit-index (WIP)
- Design mockups: https://drive.company/designs/audit-epochal-ui.png
- PoC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-epochal-poc (branch: staged-snapshots)
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1427 (WIP snapshot writer)
- Compliance dashboard prototype: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/compliance/audit-manifests

Acceptance criteria:
- Snapshot writer produces signed manifests and immutable segments for >=90% of audit event types in staging.
- Compliance verification job validates manifests and proofs end-to-end on staging for 14 consecutive days.
- Console surfaces epoch list and allows download of manifest and sample proof for any epoch.

Potential follow-ups (post-MVP):
- Compact range proofs for multi-event queries to reduce verification size.
- Cross-epoch aggregation and differential proofs for efficient long-range audits.
- Optional anchoring of manifest roots to third-party notarization services for additional customer trust.
